newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Engil seen hitting 1,800 esc in six mths.
newsitem.headline: Engil seen hitting 1,800 esc in six mths.

text.p: Shares in Portuguese construction company Engil could surpass 1,700 escudos in the coming days and 1,800 escudos within the next six months due to optimism over the company's performance in a healthy sector, analysts said.

"1,700 escudos is a barrier to break in the coming days and, within the next six months, I would not be surprised if the share headed towards 1,900 escudos," said Miguel Viana, analyst with Tottadealer.
Jose Freire, director of Lisbon broker ESR, said: "By the end of the year Engil should break through 1,700 escudos and within the next six months should surpass 1,800."
Engil shares stood at 1,665 escudos, up five, in heavy volume of 297,200 shares on Lisbon bourse at 1620 GMT.
Analysts said Engil's strong fundamentals and firm growth in the construction sector, expected to exceed Portugal's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth in 1997, favoured the stock.
It would also benefit from a climate of falling interest rates and inflation, they said.

In the first six months of 1996, Engil's consolidated net profit stood at 616 million escudos, up from 586 million in the same year-ago period. The company has forecast full year 1996 profits of 1.5 billion escudos.

ESR's Freire said: "For 1996 we expect Engil to post a consolidated net profit of around 1.5 billion escudos and for 1997 between 1.8 and 1.9 billion escudos, without being too optimistic. It is quite likely the company could post an even higher profit."
Tottadealer's Viana forecast that Engil would post a profit of 1.6 billion escudos in 1996 and 1.9 billion in 1997.
An analyst with an investment bank said: "In recent years the construction sector suffered a lot due to insufficient stimulus at the macroeconomic level and this disappointed many investors."
He added: "Engil suffered a lot because of this and so the stock looks cheap now."
Freire said: "In historical terms, construction stocks are cheap and so the sector is going to enter a golden period in the remainder of 1996 and 1997."
The investment bank analyst said: "The sector is already growing very strongly -- well above GDP -- and will continue to do so, at least until the end of 1997."
The 1997 budget forecasts GDP growth of between 2.75 and 3.25 percent in 1997, compared with about 2.8 percent this year.
